site_name: Microsoft AVC17, Lakeside Commerce Park, 39 Commerce Drive, Boydton mailing address (near Clarksville), VA 23917
verification: Refused on session review (2026-11-11). The local news page ties to the site by park name only and says the campus is being developed; Mecklenburg County assesses $466M of structures there with a first structure built in 2024, and Virginia DEQ lists the AVC17 registration (53086) as Operating. A campus can be under development while its first building runs, so no status is applied. Verifier's finding, not applied: Basis is a local news status report, not an opening report (no closer enum value). Two SoVaNOW pages agree. The Nov 4, 2026 article also says "Microsoft is building a data center near Clarksville, and the town is its water utility" and contrasts it with "One other data center operates in Mecklenburg County near Clarksville". The July 29, 2026 article says the water job will connect the plants to "the Microsoft facility under construction at Lakeside Commerce Park". Caveat: neither page says outright "not yet operating"; the verdict rests on "being built / being developed / under construction" wording in 2026, and no sentence on either page says any Microsoft building there is online. I am uncertain whether a first building of a multi-building campus could already be live; the pages do not address that. Confidence is medium for that reason. The quote is one verbatim segment of a longer sentence (the fetch tool returned it in segments).

site_name: Serverfarm TiTAN data center (Ask.com / RS Titan), 4949 Randolph Rd NE, Moses Lake, WA 98837
year_evidence_quote: Fennewald spoke about why his company decided to locate in Moses Lake, Washington, where it opened a new data center in December.
year_site_match: Tie is by campus name, not address. DCK (July 12, 2007) says Ask.com "will build a data center at the TITAN complex in Moses Lake, Washington"; Columbia Basin Herald (May 25, 2011) calls Ask.com Titan's tenant; DCK (April 22, 2011) and Serverfarm's own page identify Serverfarm's TiTAN facility in Moses Lake. No page I opened gives the street address 4949 Randolph Rd NE.
verification: Bracket: DCK dated Dec 14, 2007 says Moses Lake is "where Ask.com is building a data center" (not yet open); the blog post dated Feb 26, 2008 says it opened "in December". The only December between those dates is December 2007, and a July 2007 DCK page ("will build") rules out an earlier December. The year is not stated outright on any page, so medium, not high. The blog post is a secondhand relay of a DCK post that itself relayed a Columbia Basin Herald report; I could not open either original (the DCK link resolves to an archive index, the 2008 Herald URL returns 404). The quote was returned by the fetch tool as two overlapping verbatim segments, which I joined; the joined length (129 characters) matches the length the tool reported for the full sentence. Address 4949 Randolph Rd NE is unconfirmed by any opened page. The Ask.com data center was a fit-out inside an existing building (Serverfarm's page says the building was a command center for the Titan missile program), so 2007 dates the first data center operation at the site, not the building's construction.
